title_clean: The Lost Decade in Stock Market
summary: Uses Japan's Nikkei (about 40,000 in 1989, still ~20,000+ three decades later) to warn that equity indices can stay underwater not just for years but for decades; investors must respect this when sizing long-term bets.
lessons: Markets can go negative not just for years but for decades - Japan's Nikkei never reclaimed its 1989 peak even 30 years later.
Survival and sizing matter more than optimism when investing for the very long term.

title_clean: Crypto Options Strategy: Paired Bearish and Bullish Combos
summary: Reviews a bearish BTC combo (long 22,000PE vs short 15,000/25,000/30,000 strikes) that stayed near breakeven as BTC rallied 19,000 to 21,500, then adds a premium-funded bullish combo (long 20,000CE vs short 27,000CE x3 and 16,000PE x2) plus extra short puts to balance the book.
lessons: Run paired slightly-bearish and slightly-bullish combos so one side profits whichever way volatility breaks.
Fund a long option by selling wider strikes so net cash outlay is near zero.
Adjust by selling extra puts below the range when the market drifts toward your long strike.

strategies.name: Paired BTC combos (bearish + bullish)
strategies.construction: Bearish: buy 22,000PE (1000 qty), sell 25,000CE, 30,000CE, 15,000PE. Bullish: buy 20,000CE (~$2,800), sell 27,000CE x3 (~$600 each), sell 16,000PE x2 (~$450 each)
strategies.numbers: Bullish combo net debit ~$100 (2800 paid vs 2700 collected); earlier bearish combo ~$1,000 profit at peak; BTC 19,000->21,500 in a week
strategies.best_regime: Wide two-sided uncertainty with high IV; define comfort band roughly 16,000-27,000
strategies.adjustments: Sold additional 18,000/17,000/16,000 puts to offset the losing leg's drift; keep adjusting toward expiry
strategies.risks: Loss if BTC breaks below ~16,000 or above ~27,000; crypto exchange counterparty risk; high IV means fast premium swings

title_clean: Fake MTM Screenshots: Why Verification theater Fails
summary: Dismantles the MTM-verification trend: paired long/short accounts guarantee one winning screenshot, verifiers can be bribed, and a single-day MTM proves nothing. Proposes broker read-only logins and audited multi-year P&L as the real fixes; lifestyle and filings reveal real profits.
lessons: A one-day MTM screenshot proves nothing - only multi-month realized P&L does.
Paired long/short accounts always produce one verifiable winner, defeating any screenshot check.
Verifiers themselves can be bribed; who verifies the verifier?
If brokers offered read-only logins, anyone could audit a trader's real P&L and the scam would die.
Real profits show up in lifestyle and audited filings, not screenshots.

strategies.name: Read-only broker access (proposed fix)
strategies.construction: Brokers issue a second read-only username/password for the back office; claimants share it publicly so anyone can inspect realized P&L and MTM
strategies.best_regime: Industry-wide: would eliminate fake-screenshot and paired-account fraud
strategies.risks: Requires broker implementation; privacy concerns for those with multiple businesses

title_clean: Nifty 21K or 35K: The Medium-Term Bull Case
summary: Debunks his own 35,000 clickbait: 2008 and 2020 crashes fell 50%/40% before doubling, but 2022's dip was under 20% and the Fed is tightening, not easing. Builds the bull case on the wall of worry, markets leading the economy by 6-12 months, capital-goods strength as a lead indicator, and rupee stabilization; sets targets 18,500-19,000 (Dec-22) and 20,500-21,000 (Dec-23).
lessons: Bull markets climb the wall of worry - buy when there is trouble, sell when all is well.
Markets price in known problems 6-12 months before they resolve; by the time bad news lands, the market may rally.
Capital-goods outperformance (L&T, BHEL) is a 6-12 month lead indicator of economic expansion, as before the 2004-08 bull run.
After a bad calendar year, the following year tends to deliver above-average returns.
A crash needs a 40-50% drawdown plus QE to double; a 20% dip under quantitative tightening does not support repeat-doubling targets.

title_clean: BTC Short Strangle Amid the FTX Crash
summary: With FTX's bankruptcy crushing crypto (BTC ~70,000 to ~15-16,000) while equities recovered, sells a wide BTC short strangle - 10,000PE near ~$340 and 25,000CE near ~$280 for ~$620 total - collecting the 10,000-25,000 range; teaches live order-book tactics and repeats the exchange-risk cap of ~10% of capital.
lessons: Simple short strangles in high-IV markets can beat complex structures; wide breakevens are the cushion.
Work limit orders through the order book - start beyond the best quote and walk toward it.
Exchange failure (FTX) is a bigger crypto risk than price movement; cap per-exchange exposure and diversify venues.
Post-crash, surviving platforms consolidate the business like TCS/Infosys did after the dot-com bust.
You make small small profits - that is how option sellers survive.

title_clean: Bharat Bond: Yield, Tax Math and the Pledging Trick
summary: Presents the December 2022 Bharat Bond tranche (7.5% indicative YTM, April 2033): explains the FD-vs-bond tax arbitrage (slab-taxed interest vs 20% LTCG with indexation on a zero-coupon structure), the SLR framework, AAA PSU credit, lowest expense ratio, and the trader's trick of pledging Bharat Bond ETFs as collateral to earn yield and trading margin simultaneously; teaches bond-price mechanics with a three-story FD parable.
lessons: Hold-to-maturity bond funds remove mark-to-market anxiety: interim price dips don't change the promised yield.
Bond prices fall when interest rates rise and rise when rates fall - the three-story FD parable.
Zero-coupon bond funds convert slab-taxed interest into indexation-benefit capital gains for high-bracket investors.
Pledging bond ETFs as collateral earns yield and trading margin at once - a structural edge over FDs.
Judge any instrument by Safety, Liquidity, Return - in that order.

strategies.best_regime: High-rate environments locking long tenure; traders wanting low-risk collateral with yield
strategies.adjustments: If pledged funds are needed, buy in secondary market (instant pledge) at the cost of transaction charges
strategies.risks: Interest-rate mark-to-market before maturity; 1-2 month pledge-eligibility lag for new tranches; small credit risk despite AAA

title_clean: The Long-Dated Options Combo from the Conference Circuit
summary: Walks through a Dec-2023-expiry combo demoed at conferences: long 16,000CE (2,450), short 2x 20,000CE (700 each) and short 3x 13,000PE (~285-300) for net debit ~150; the short puts collapsed to ~60 and were squared off, then rolled to 15,000PE for ~2.75 lakh more - total ~3.4 lakh as Nifty rallied and VIX collapsed 20-21 to 12-13. Frames Buffett's LEAPS selling and Nov-Feb as the long-dated sweet spot.
lessons: Long-dated combos let trend plus falling IV compound; both tailwinds stacked in late 2022.
When a short leg collapses toward zero quickly, square it off and redeploy closer to the money (rolled 13,000PE to 15,000PE).
November-February is the best window to initiate long-dated option structures.
30-40% a year is a realistic long-dated target; the demo's bigger profit was an extraordinary VIX-collapse bonus.
Far-expiry options are illiquid - size positions small.

strategies.numbers: Net debit ~150; later short 13,000PE fell 285->60 (2 lots squared off), rolled to 15,000PE for ~2.75 lakh additional; running profit ~3.4 lakh; VIX 20-21 -> 12-13; benchmark expectation 30-40% p.a.

strategies.risks: Illiquidity in far strikes; a VIX spike instead of collapse would hurt; unlimited put-side loss if index crashes
